prerequisites: Knowledge of stationary and quasi-stationary electromagnetism studied in physics courses.
Theory of electrical circuits from Electrical Engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Development of competencies related to static and electromechanical conversion of electrical energy and non-linear circuits.
Basic elements for the analysis of static and rotating electrical machines and static converters of electrical energy.
Operating principles of static and rotating electrical machines and power electronic circuits.
Steady-state analysis methods for transformers and main AC and DC motors and equivalent steady-state circuits.
Analysis methods for circuits for static conversion of electrical energy for motor control and for the exploitation of electrical energy production systems from renewable sources.
Selection methods for transformers, AC and DC motors, and conversion apparatus.
Ability to analyze a transformer in steady-state.
Ability to analyze the main AC and DC motors.
Ability to choose a transformer or a motor suitable for a given application.
Ability to simulate the qualitative behavior of the electrical machine or static converter using computer software.

syllabus_topics: Review of stationary and quasi-stationary electromagnetism in material media, frequency analysis, complements of circuit theory
The transformer: operating principle, circuit model, efficiency, tests, parallel operation, three-phase transformers

The asynchronous motor: rotating field, characteristic equations and equivalent circuit, mechanical and electromechanical characteristics, starting and speed regulation, braking. Double-cage motor. Single-phase asynchronous motor.

The synchronous machine and the DC machine: operating principles, equivalent circuits, mechanical and electromechanical characteristics, starting and speed regulation, braking, excitation. Brushless, stepper, permanent magnet motors.
Static energy conversion and regulation circuits: main topologies for DC/DC, DC/AC, AC/DC conversion, PWM modulation, simulations.
Rechargeable batteries: operating principle, characteristics, circuit models, computer simulations.
Elements of electrical safety: distribution of electrical energy in low voltage, overvoltages, overcurrents, protection against direct and indirect contact.
Applications to systems based on renewable energy sources (photovoltaic, wind, fuel cells): modeling, analysis and solution of control and energy conversion problems.
teaching_methods: Use of circuit simulation and calculation software

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam (discussion of theoretical/applied topics and homework solutions)

assessment_rules: The oral exam, lasting 30 minutes, requires the student to present two theoretical or applied course topics chosen by the professor and discuss the solutions to group homework assignments. A minimum score of 18 is given for uncertainties in problem-solving methods and limited knowledge of main machines. A maximum score of 30 is given for complete and in-depth knowledge, efficient and accurate problem-solving, and strong ability to connect properties of different electrical machines and components. Honors (Lode) are awarded for significant mastery, excellent language, and independent elaboration in diverse contexts.
